changes.text: 作者推断，这套流程的要害在于它不依赖任何人相信谁的品格：仪式前一日成文，次日按议定次序进行，凭证当场易手，讲稿副本随凭证一并交出。（据日志，委任状是交给议长的。议定稿第4条的方括号增字加入了“委任状”和“交给议长”的字样，但正文中把讲稿副本交给副官、再呈给秘书的字样仍在。本篇所据的OCR文本在这一处同样有乱码，无法判断这些字是否已被删去。第6条由秘书接收委任状的字样，情况相同。）一个人是否忠诚，一场仪式无法证明；但权力是否已归位，可以在这一天被记成白纸黑字。这是作者对记录方式的解释，日志本身并未陈述其用意。

The author's inference is that the point of the procedure was that it depended on nobody's character. The order was written the day before and followed the next day, the token changed hands on the spot, and a copy of the address was handed over along with it. (The journal has the commission delivered to the President. The bracketed insertions in clause 4 of the draft add the words for the commission and for delivery to the President, but the wording that has the copy of the address going to his aide to be presented to the secretary remains in the printed text. The OCR text this piece relies on is garbled at that point too and cannot show whether those words were struck out. The same holds for the wording in clause 6 in which the secretary receives the commission.) A man's loyalty cannot be proven by a ceremony. Whether power has been put back where it belongs, however, can be entered in black and white on a particular day. That is an interpretation of how the record was made; the journal itself states no such intention.

本篇所据只有《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录：12月20日至23日的记录，包括12月22日议定的接见次序、23日的接见经过与讲话文本。没有取得任何在场者的私人记述，因此讲话者的神情与语气、在场个人的现场反应，本篇都无从得知。日志记动作、记次序、记讲话，不描写个人的神情与现场反应。讲话本身说到他对独立与主权得到确认感到欣慰，对合众国有机会成为受尊重的国家感到高兴；国会的正式答词也自称怀着难以言表的感情接受。但这些是写成文字的正式表态，答词更是机构的书面表态，不是对现场的描写。本篇也不涉及他此后的事。凡是原文没写的动机、念头和“他考虑过的选项”，本篇都不替他补。

Everything in this piece rests on one source: the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 — the record of December 20 to 23, including the order of audience agreed on December 22, the audience of the twenty-third, and the text of the address. No private account by anyone present was consulted, and so the speaker's face and tone, and the reactions of individuals in the room, are beyond what this piece can know. The journal records gestures, sequence, and speech; it does not describe individual faces or reactions in the room. The address itself speaks of his being happy at the confirmation of independence and sovereignty, and pleased with the opportunity afforded the United States of becoming a respectable nation. Congress's formal answer speaks of receiving his resignation with emotions too affecting for utterance. But these are formal statements set down in writing, the answer being the institution's own written statement, not descriptions of the scene. Nor does this piece follow the man beyond that day. Motives, private thoughts, and options he may have considered are never supplied by this writer where the source is silent.

dispositions.rationale: 删去“与日志所记一致/which matches the journal”。括号说明改为：第4条的方括号增字加入了委任状和交给议长的字样，但把讲稿副本交给副官、再呈给秘书的正文字样仍在，OCR在此处同样有乱码，无法判断是否已删去。第6条由秘书接收委任状的字样，情况相同。这样与limits.1的保留一致。中英同步修改。

evidence.quote: copy of his address to hia aid to be pre acntod to the Scorotaiy [to the President]
the words in brackets being in the writing of Elias Boudinot

dispositions.rationale: 修正对讲话的转述，中英同步。按原文，欣慰（happy）针对独立与主权得到确认，高兴（pleased）针对合众国获得成为受尊重国家的机会，不再把两者都挂在“独立得到确认”上。

evidence.quote: Happy in the confirmation of our independence and sovereignty, and pleased with the opportunity afforded the United States, of becoming a respectable nation
